name: obsidian-skills
description: Agent skills for Obsidian. Teach your agent to use Obsidian CLI and open formats including Markdown, Bases, JSON Canvas.
readmeExcerpt:
Agent Skills for use with Obsidian.

These skills follow the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) so they can be used by any skills-compatible agent, including Claude Code, Codex, and Open Code.

## Installation

### Claude Code marketplace

From terminal:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
claude plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills
```

From within a Claude Code session:

```sh
/plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
/plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills
```

To get new skills later, run `claude plugin update obsidian@obsidian-skills`.

### Codex marketplace

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
```

Then install Obsidian from the plugin directory in Codex or the ChatGPT desktop app.

### Cursor

Install Obsidian from the [Cursor Marketplace](https://cursor.com/marketplace).

### npx skills

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
```

To use ssh instead, if you have a GitHub SSH key set up:

```sh
npx skills add git@github.com:obsidianmd/obsidian-skills.git
```

### Manually

#### Claude Code

Copy the `plugins/obsidian/skills/` directory to `.claude/skills/` in the root of your Obsidian vault (or whichever folder you're using with Claude Code). See more in the [official Claude Skills documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview).

#### Codex

Copy the `plugins/obsidian/skills/` directory into your Codex skills path (typically `~/.agents/skills`). See the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) for the standard skill format.

#### OpenCode

Clone the entire repo into the OpenCode skills directory (`~/.opencode/skills/`):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills.git ~/.opencode/skills/obsidian-skills
```

Do not copy only the inner `skills/` folder — clone the full repo so the directory structure is `~/.opencode/skills/obsidian-skills/plugins/obsidian/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.

OpenCode auto-discovers all `SKILL.md` files under `~/.opencode/skills/`. No changes to `opencode.json` or any config file are needed. Skills become available after restarting OpenCode.

## Release maintenance

Update the plugin version in every manifest with:

```sh
./scripts/bump.sh patch
```

The script also accepts `major`, `minor`, or an explicit version like `1.1.0`.

## Skills

| Skill                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [obsidian-markdown](plugins/obsidian/skills/obsidian-markdown) | Create and edit [Obsidian Flavored Markdown](https://help.obsidian.md/obsidian-flavored-markdown) (`.md`) with wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties, and other Obsidian-specific syntax |
| [obsidian-bases](plugins/obsidian/skills/obsidian-bases)       | Create and edit [Obsidian Bases](https://help.obsidian.md/bases/syntax) (`.base`) with views, filters, formulas, and summaries                                                             |
| [json-canvas](plugins/obsidian/skills/json-canvas)             | Create and edit [JSON Canvas](https://jsoncanvas.org/) files (`.canvas`) with nodes, edges, groups, and connections                                                                        |
| [obsidian-cli](plugins/obsidian/skills/obsidian-cli)           | Interact with Obsidian vaults via the [Obsidian CLI](https://help.obsidian.md/cli) including plugin and theme development                                                                  |
| [obsidian-headless](plugins/obsidian/skills/obsidian-headless) | Sync and publish vaults from the command line with [Obsidian Headless](https://help.obsidian.md/headless), without the desktop app                                                         |
| [defuddle](plugins/obsidian/skills/defuddle)                   | Extract clean markdown from web pages using [Defuddle](https://github.com/kepano/defuddle), removing clutter to save tokens                                                                |
| [knap](plugins/obsidian/skills/knap)                           | Render Markdown templates from JSON or CSV data using [Knap](https://github.com/obsidianmd/knap), including batch file generation                                                          |

releases.body:
Obsidian Skills is now one plugin for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, published by Obsidian. The repository moved to `obsidianmd/obsidian-skills`, and old links redirect.

If you installed from the Claude Code marketplace, run `claude plugin update obsidian@obsidian-skills`. Earlier changes, including the Knap skill, didn't reach existing installs because the version stayed at 1.0.1 (#146). `scripts/bump.sh` now sets the version in every manifest.

### Plugin

- Moved the skills to `plugins/obsidian/skills/`.
- Added Codex and Cursor marketplaces next to the Claude one (#110, #142).
- Added a plugin icon, README and license for the Claude, Codex, ChatGPT and Cursor directories.

### Skills

- Obsidian CLI: `content=` converts every `\n` and `\t` with no escape, so the skill writes content with backslashes, such as LaTeX, directly to the file.
- Obsidian CLI: documented how the CLI picks a vault, exit status 0 on errors, the update-links dialog that `rename` and `move` wait on, dots in file names, and `rename`, `move` and `delete` (#131, #132).
- Obsidian CLI, Defuddle, Knap: check that the tool is installed and ask before installing it.
- Markdown: escape alias pipes in tables, quot

aiSummary.oneLiner: Agent Skills allowing autonomous AI coding assistants to interact with and manage Obsidian vaults directly.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Obsidian Skills provides a bridge between modern AI coding agents and the popular personal knowledge management tool, Obsidian. It adheres to the standardized Agent Skills specification, offering a suite of programmatic tools that agents can utilize to interact with the vault ecosystem. The repository contains specialized scripts and configurations that allow agents like Claude Code or Cursor to read, write, and organize markdown files seamlessly. This enables AI assistants to act as intelligent co-pilots within a user's knowledge base, automating tasks like note formatting, metadata extraction, or complex link generation. By exposing Obsidian's structure to autonomous agents, it significantly extends the capabilities of traditional note-taking workflows.
keyFeatures: Standardized specification: Adheres strictly to the Agent Skills protocol for out-of-the-box compatibility with major coding agents.
Vault manipulation: Allows agents to programmatically create, read, update, and delete markdown files within the Obsidian structure.
Seamless integration: Designed to be easily installed via package managers or direct git sourcing for rapid workflow setup.
Metadata management: Equips agents with the ability to safely parse and modify YAML frontmatter across multiple documents.
Automated organization: Provides the foundational tools needed for an AI to restructure folders or generate dynamic indexes.

useCases.title: Automated refactoring
useCases.description: Command an AI agent to mass-update outdated frontmatter schemas across hundreds of notes simultaneously.

useCases.title: Content synthesis
useCases.description: Instruct a coding assistant to read an entire folder of meeting notes and generate a comprehensive summary document with bidirectional links.

useCases.title: Workflow automation
useCases.description: Utilize an agent to automatically format unorganized raw text dumps into clean, structured markdown adhering to specific templates.

useCases.title: Knowledge retrieval
useCases.description: Allow an AI to search through the vault structure using complex programmatic logic to find obscure, interconnected data points.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers and power users who utilize both Obsidian for knowledge management and AI agents for workflow automation. It is particularly helpful for knowledge workers aiming to create complex, automated personal knowledge management systems.
